purpose: Development-only rule-table vs witness-export diagnosis; no new manually authored reference

reference.builder: scripts/run_gamespec_boundary_panel.py package; use all existing cases, static_visibility, dynamic_visibility and ALL change_witnesses, byte/hash equality checked
reference.independence_limit: Frozen reference predates this model run; developer-authored v7 truth, not external human review or proof of natural-language truth

models.inherit: v7 selected v4 f1_s1 actual API parameters, including strict proposal schema, no API seed added

A.description: Unchanged v7 direct task. Exact original messages, proposal JSON schema and serializer; no table.

B.description: One reply with stage_table only; deterministic program derives a legacy proposal without seeing any reference. If visibility changes, use unchanged change_witnesses(table)[0]; if constant, derive owners from visibility membership. A never-visible constant field cannot be assigned in legacy three-owner language and yields explicit derivation failure.
B.task_instruction: For this diagnostic output only stage_table: the visible-field sets at the FIRST and SECOND modeled decisions, with player 0 then player 1 at each decision. Use the given field vocabulary. A program will derive the legacy proposal from this table. Do not output a decision, candidates or witness.

C.description: One reply declares stage_table first and proposal second. Model supplies both based on its own interpretation; proposal goes through unchanged serializer and main scorers. One structured reply does not prove internal reasoning order.
C.task_instruction: For this diagnostic output stage_table first, then proposal. stage_table lists visible fields at the FIRST and SECOND modeled decisions, with player 0 then player 1 at each decision. Form the legacy decision/candidates/witness proposal using YOUR OWN declared table. Use the given field vocabulary. Do not use or invent a reference table.

interface.system_and_source_priority: byte-identical v4 f1_s1 system and source-priority strings in all conditions
interface.common_user_content: exact original v7 RULES/fields/task prefix before the appended Proposal JSON schema; no witnesses, reference tables, reference owners or case labels in requests
interface.necessary_difference: A is byte-identical original prompt/schema. B/C replace only final schema block and append frozen output-task instruction. Different outputs cannot literally share one schema; no post-result condition-specific tuning.
interface.stage_table_reference_shape: [[player0_visible_fields, player1_visible_fields] at first decision, [player0_visible_fields, player1_visible_fields] at second decision]; static duplicates existing v7 static_visibility
interface.instantiate: replace $FROZEN_CASE_FIELDS by the exact existing case field vocabulary; use items min/max fixed 2 for phase/player axes; reject duplicates/unknown fields offline; list order has no semantic effect
interface.no_new_reference_or_output_normalization: do not change field names/players or repair malformed outputs to obtain a pass

schedule.case_order: exact v7 scope_case_order (12 instances, six static/dynamic pairs)
schedule.order: case index then repeat 0..4; rotate A/B/C by (case_index + repeat)%3 to reduce fixed order confounding, identical plan for both models

scoring.legacy: Every A proposal, B program-derived proposal and C declared proposal uses unchanged v5 score: original v4 semantics + direct v5 table oracle. Any disagreement stops and journals counterexample. Same legacy pass criterion across all conditions.
scoring.table: Strict shape/vocabulary/duplicate validation then exact per-phase/player visible SET equality to frozen v7 reference; record every missing/extra cell; no table grading in A.
scoring.B_program: reference-free deterministic export, no fallback to reference, no best-witness selection using truth. Table wrong but valid witness correct is separately reported.
scoring.C_self_consistency: Compare proposal to own declared table as well as frozen reference. Correct-table/wrong-reference-witness counted with conditional and assigned denominators; separate schema/transport errors from valid-schema semantic export errors.
scoring.whole_response: Additional table correctness in B/C reported separately, not used to silently redefine legacy witness correctness. Every table/legacy/interface failure retained.
scoring.witness_denominator: dynamic instances only: 6 pairs x5=30 assigned per condition/model. Static correctness separately 30; table correctness both 60 and dynamic-only30.
scoring.pairing: match case_id/repeat across A/B/C for descriptive discordance, no claim of shared API randomness
scoring.overlap: Labels can overlap; count failed trials independently and do not sum labels as failures.

required: all case/condition/repeat raw replies and offline rescoring
B table correctness and exported witness correctness
C table correctness, witness correctness, table-correct/witness-wrong ratio including exact denominators and valid-interface subset
A-wrong/B-right matched trial list and rule-instance summaries

statistics.unit: six dynamic rule pairs, average five technical repeats within each pair; not 30 independent rules
comparisons: B-A dynamic witness correctness for Luna
C-A dynamic witness correctness for Luna
B-A dynamic witness correctness for Sol
C-A dynamic witness correctness for Sol
statistics.test: exploratory exact paired sign-flip over 2^6 pair-level differences, two-sided absolute mean difference; ties included; Holm-adjust four p-values at 0.05
statistics.limits: purposive six reused development rules, nonrandom condition assignment and nonidentical output demands; sign-flip exchangeability is an assumption, not population or formal causal evidence; report raw differences even with no significance

analysis.attribution: B>A supports utility of decomposition+deterministic export, but alone cannot identify the latent error layer. C correct table + valid but self-inconsistent/wrong witness gives direct output-level export evidence. Incorrect emitted table gives understanding/representation-stage evidence, not proof of hidden cognition. C>A supports explicit-table elicitation benefit, not cognitive mechanism causality.
analysis.decision_rule: Judge whether stage-table path deserves continued development from its measured per-model errors, direct evidence and resource costs; no automatic model switch or trial advancement; inconclusive if ceiling or no error opportunities.

resources.prices: frozen v4 uncached price estimates; log actual provider usage/reasoning/latency, unknown-usage costs flagged as reserved estimates
resources.cost_scope: No cost-based sample-size reduction. Existing anomaly guards exceed maximum planned cost under token caps (Sol 180x$0.045=$8.10 below $10 guard; Luna180x$0.00225=$0.405 below $2 guard).
resources.stop_rules: Stop affected model on any provider exception/timeout, refusal, missing usage, model/token/anomaly mismatch; retain all assigned denominators and unexecuted trials. No automatic retries. Truncation/schema/semantic failure is retained and next planned trial continues. Oracle disagreement immediately preserves counterexample and stops that model; do not launch further dispatch after detecting disagreement.
resources.audit_before_call: First commit this preregistration; then implementation/tests/full verification, immutable source/reference/bundle/schema hashes and a second commit before any model generation; validate committed bytes before dispatch.
